title: Remove Letter To Equalize Frequency
statement: You get a string `word` of lowercase letters. You must delete exactly one character from it (skipping the deletion is not allowed). Return `true` if some deletion leaves a string in which every letter that still appears occurs the same number of times, and `false` if no deletion achieves that. A letter's frequency is how many times it occurs; letters that no longer appear are ignored.
constraints: word contains only lowercase English letters
notes:
## Intuition

Only the letter counts matter, not their positions: deleting any copy of a letter has the same effect. So instead of trying all positions, try each of the at most 26 distinct letters. For each one, lower its count by one and check whether all the counts that are still above zero agree. The brute force (delete every index and recount) gives the same answer in O(n²).

## Approach

1. Build `count`, the number of times each of the 26 letters appears in `word`.
2. For each `letter` that appears, take one copy away by decrementing `count[letter]`.
3. Collect the counts that are still positive into `present` and set `allEqual` if they all match the first one.
4. Put the copy back so the next trial starts from the original counts.
5. If any trial gave `allEqual`, return `true`; after all 26 letters, return `false`.

## Example 1, step by step

`word = "abcc"` gives counts `a: 1, b: 1, c: 2`. Removing an `a` leaves `b: 1, c: 2`, not equal; removing a `b` leaves `a: 1, c: 2`, not equal. Removing a `c` leaves `a: 1, b: 1, c: 1`, so `allEqual` is true and the answer is `true`.

## Complexity

- Time: O(n + 26²): one pass to count, then 26 trials over 26 counts each.
- Space: O(1): the count array has a fixed 26 slots.

## Pitfalls

- A letter whose count drops to zero disappears; it must not be compared, which is why only positive counts go into `present`.
- Shortcut rules ("the most frequent letter must be one higher") miss cases such as a single letter like `"aa"` or a letter that appears once, like `"abbcc"`. Trying every letter avoids them.
- Restore the count after each trial, or later trials see a damaged frequency table.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `count` | how many times each letter `a` to `z` appears |
| `letter` | index 0 to 25 of the letter being removed in this trial |
| `present` | counts of the letters still in the word after the removal |
| `allEqual` | whether every count in `present` is the same |
